office_explainer: One of six council members who, with the mayor, set the city budget, tax rate and local laws.
why_it_matters: Council Member Shane Scott seeks another term against Heather Hunter.

candidates.name: Shane Scott
candidates.background: Current San Marcos City Council member for Place 4 (Community Impact).

own_words.text: Removing red tape and addressing the utility cost on payers.
I voted against data centers and was concerned about how much power and water they use.
Names affordable housing as the city's greatest challenge over the next five years.

candidates.name: Heather Hunter
candidates.background: Project manager specializing in grants, with degrees in political science and political management (Community Impact).

own_words.text: My top priorities are the environment, affordable housing, and supporting local and small businesses.
No economic benefit outweighs protecting our river and aquifer.
Says her grant-writing experience would help the city go after outside money it is now leaving on the table.

scope_plain: Every City of San Marcos voter
office_explainer: One of six council members who, with the mayor, set the city budget, tax rate and local laws.
why_it_matters: Special election for the rest of Amanda Rodriguez’s term. She is running for mayor.

candidates.name: Lisa Prewitt
candidates.background: Small business owner and former San Marcos City Council member (Community Impact).

own_words.text: Protecting the Edwards Aquifer, our springs, and the San Marcos River.
Making growth pay for itself instead of raising residents’ rates.
Would defend the city's ban on data centers and wants any large water or energy user to cover its own infrastructure costs.

candidates.name: Bill Miller
candidates.background: Served 10.5 years in the U.S. Coast Guard; business owner and farmer/rancher (Community Impact).

own_words.text: my top priorities would be food security, protecting our natural resources, and affordable housing
I will never agree with having data centers inside the city of San Marcos.
Worries the city will not keep up with population growth and wants growth balanced with protecting what makes it great.

candidates.name: Juan Miguel Arredondo
candidates.background: United Way CEO, San Marcos CISD trustee, Housing Authority commissioner and former legislative chief of staff (Community Impact).

own_words.text: My priorities are affordability and stronger neighborhoods.
I support the city’s prohibition on data centers.
Would focus on safe, affordable housing, utility and basic-needs help, good-paying jobs, and streets, sidewalks and drainage.
